label: input q during the copy phase
explanation: Fires only when the fed-back input token is q during the copy phase (t > L), i.e. while the model is outputting the original token after a q. Never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on any other input token; dev recall 1.0, precision 0.87. Magnitude is largest when q is copied at recall_idx 2-4 (2-4 steps after <DEL>, e.g. original sequences like d q ... / 1 m q ...); weak at recall_idx 1 (q as first token, rate 0.02) and later positions; a repeated q later in the copy is usually weaker. Remaining false positives are mostly q at the first copy step or a second q in the sequence. Adding recall_idx >= 2 raises precision to 0.93 but lowers F1.

issues: Checked on the test split: the feature never fires outside the copy phase and never fires on any copy-phase input other than q. The predicate has recall 1.0, mass recall 1.0, 0 missed activations and precision 0.872. The core claims hold.

One factual error: the explanation says q right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1) fires at rate 0.02. That 0.02 is the rate over all input tokens at recall_idx 1. Restricted to q, recall_idx==1 has precision 0.61, so the feature fires on 61% of those q's. The activations there are weak, though: they carry only 4% of the activation mass and sit almost entirely in the bottom two quartiles. So 'weak at recall_idx 1' is right, but 'rarely fires' is wrong.

False positives are partly systematic: about 6.5k of the 11.6k test false positives come from q at recall_idx 1, which the explanation already admits. The rest are spread across later positions, often q near the end of the copy, with no clean cut. Adding to_go>=1 raises precision to 0.96 but drops recall to 0.70. Adding in_count==1 does not raise precision over recall_idx>=2 alone (0.931 vs 0.931), so 'a repeated q is weaker' is not a strong effect for firing (in_count>=2 precision 0.85, about the same as the base rate).
The recall_idx>=2 refinement scores test P 0.931 / R 0.872 / F1 0.901, which is below the base predicate's 0.932. Keeping the simpler predicate is justified.
Magnitude claim checked: recall_idx 2-4 holds 80% of the mass, and the top examples have q at copy positions 2-3. Confirmed.
